sources.agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
sources.report: 2022 Viral Hepatitis Surveillance Report — Table 2.5: Newly Reported Cases of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection
sources.metric: Newly Reported Chronic Hepatitis B: 364 cases, 33.3 per 100,000 population (ranked among highest state rates in US)
sources.important_note: In the CDC 2021 Table 2.5, Rhode Island data was listed as unavailable. The 364 case count / 33.3 rate is definitively from the 2022 report.

sources.mandate: Mandatory reporting of positive maternal HBsAg within 4 working days; Universal newborn birth dose within 24 hours

epidemiological_classification.metric_type: Newly reported chronic cases (surveillance notification incidence)
epidemiological_classification.total_prevalent_infections_note: 364 represents newly reported surveillance cases in 2022, NOT total prevalent active infections in Rhode Island. Total state chronic HBV prevalence is estimated at 3,000-8,000+ individuals, many undiagnosed.
